name: EU Web Accessibility Directive
standard: EN 301 549 V3.2.1 (WCAG 2.1 AA for web); V4.1.1 (WCAG 2.2) published 2026-09-02 but not yet cited in the OJ

laws.summary: Member States must make public sector bodies' websites and mobile apps accessible (perceivable, operable, understandable, robust).
Sets the model accessibility statement public bodies must use.
Sets the monitoring methodology and Member State reporting arrangements.
Cites the harmonised standard (now EN 301 549 V3.2.1) that gives presumption of conformity.

policy_docs.title: Web Accessibility Directive — Standards and harmonisation

applies_to: Websites (any device) and mobile apps of public sector bodies in EU Member States: state, regional, local authorities and bodies governed by public law.

deadlines.what: Websites published on or after 2018-09-23 must comply
All other (older) public sector websites must comply
Public sector mobile apps must comply
First Member State monitoring reports due; then every 3 years

exceptions: Public service broadcasters and their subsidiaries (Art 1(3)(a))
NGOs not providing essential public services or services for persons with disabilities (Art 1(3)(b))
Office file formats published before 2018-09-23 unless needed for active administrative processes
Online maps, if essential navigational info is provided accessibly
Third-party content neither funded, developed nor controlled by the body
Heritage collection reproductions that cannot be made accessible
Extranet/intranet content published before 2019-09-23 until substantially revised
Archives not needed for active processes and not updated after 2019-09-23
Optional national exclusion: schools, kindergartens, nurseries (except essential online admin functions) (Art 1(5))
Disproportionate burden (Art 5), which must be assessed and explained in the accessibility statement
requires: Meet Art 4 accessibility requirements (presumed via EN 301 549 harmonised standard)
Publish and regularly update an accessibility statement using the 2018/1523 model (Art 7(1)); for apps, on the body's website or alongside download info
Statement must list non-accessible content with reasons and alternatives
Feedback mechanism so anyone can report failures and request excluded content
Link to the national enforcement procedure (Art 9)
Give an adequate response within a reasonable period
mobile: explicit — Art 1(2) and Art 12(3)(c) cover mobile applications of public sector bodies; apps must comply from 2021-06-23.
procurement: Directive itself does not set procurement rules; public procurement accessibility flows from Directive 2014/24/EU Art 42 and, for EAA-covered products/services, EAA Art 24. EN 301 549 is widely used as the procurement spec.
enforcement: Member States must provide an adequate and effective enforcement procedure, such as an ombudsman (Art 9); national monitoring per 2018/1524 with reports to the Commission every 3 years (Art 8).
notes: Article text read from legislation.gov.uk's copy of the EU directive (EUR-Lex blocked automated fetches). The Commission page confirms V3.2.1 is cited via Decision 2021/1339. EN 301 549 V4.1.1 (WCAG 2.2) was published by ETSI on 2026-09-02. Its OJ citation is only scheduled: one secondary source says 2026-11-30, another says 2026-12-16 per ETSI's work programme. Until it is cited, V3.2.1 remains the presumption-of-conformity standard. Several Member States already require or recommend WCAG 2.2 voluntarily.
